links.outcome: Patient comprehension of acute minor illness information at Day 14 with vs without LLM plain-language summaries
links.effect: Comprehension at Day 14 was higher with LLM summaries (Claude M=81.4, GPT-5.1 M=79.6) than control (M=63.2); F(2,169)=47.34, p<0.001, partial η2=0.36.
links.quote: LLM-embedded patient portal summaries significantly improved comprehension of acute minor illnesses and reduced unnecessary healthcare utilization in a primary care setting.

links.outcome: Accuracy and safety of LLM summaries in clinician audit of 20% of summaries
links.effect: Minor factual imprecision in 5.7% (Claude) and 11.8% (GPT-5.1) of audited summaries; zero clinically significant hallucinations.
links.quote: Minor factual imprecision rates in audited summaries were 5.7% (Claude) and 11.8% (GPT-5.1), with zero clinically significant hallucinations across all audited summaries.

unlisted_practices: Embedding LLM-generated plain-language visit summaries in a dedicated patient portal panel to improve comprehension, engagement, and reduce unnecessary return visits

screen.reason: Three-arm trial evaluating LLM-generated patient portal summaries versus standard care on patient comprehension, engagement, and utilization. It tests the intervention overall against control rather than testing a specific deployment safeguard/practice (such as comparing with vs without clinician review).
